ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Sick Visit — Rabindranath Tagore

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for fever with a urinary catheter

text.paragraph: Fever and chills since last night, with cloudy urine and a lower abdominal ache, four weeks after a urinary catheter was placed. [S]

Mr. Tagore is a 79-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia and chronic urinary retention, drained by an indwelling urethral catheter for four weeks, on tamsulosin 0.4 mg at bedtime and finasteride 5 mg daily. Since last night he has had chills, a temperature of 38.4 °C at home, an ache above the pubic bone and in the right flank, and cloudy, strong-smelling urine in the bag, with some leakage around the catheter this morning. He has had no rigors since the night, no vomiting, no breathlessness, no cough, no diarrhea, and no blood in the urine. He has eaten little today but is drinking. One of his helpers thought he was a little slow to answer in the night; this morning he is clear. He has not fallen. He has kept the bag below his bladder and washed around the catheter daily. He continues his herbal preparation. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-03-17; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Tired and flushed but alert and conversing normally
4AT score 0: alert, oriented to age, date of birth, place, and year, months backward without error; no delirium
Pulse 98, regular; blood pressure 118/68 mmHg; capillary refill under 2 seconds
Mild suprapubic tenderness; bladder not distended; mild right costovertebral angle tenderness
Catheter in place; meatus slightly red without discharge; cloudy urine in the bag

Benign prostatic hyperplasia with severe lower urinary tract symptoms (IPSS 26) and bladder outlet obstruction: prostate about 85 mL on ultrasound, smooth and benign on examination, PSA 4.9 ng/mL (PSA density 0.06)
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis linked to the retrospective enlarged-prostate reading of his last illness; the conflicting cancer claim is not adopted.
Urinary retention with severe lower urinary tract symptoms (bladder scan 640 mL after voiding) and a raised creatinine, cause under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis of benign prostatic hyperplasia with chronic retention at the two-week visit.
Chronic urinary retention from bladder outlet obstruction, low risk once drained (no hydronephrosis; creatinine normal after drainage), managed with an indwelling urethral catheter
S — Synthetic diagnosis; resolved after a successful second trial without catheter.
Catheter-associated urinary tract infection with fever, without sepsis; resolved
S — Synthetic complication of the synthetic catheter at an unscheduled visit; it echoes, without asserting, the urinary infections of his documented last illness.

Infection and inflammatory reaction due to indwelling urethral catheter, initial encounter

list.item:
Catheter-associated urinary tract infection with fever, without sepsis (T83.511A). Fever, suprapubic and flank pain, and pyuria (60 white cells per high-power field) in a man with a four-week-old catheter, with white cells 13.8 x10^3/uL: a catheter-associated urinary tract infection, probably with upper-tract involvement. There is no sign of sepsis: he is alert (4AT 0), his blood pressure is 118/68 mmHg, and his respiratory rate is 18, so treatment at home is safe with close follow-up. Creatinine 1.31 mg/dL (eGFR 55) is a little higher than two weeks ago and allows standard antibiotic doses. [S]
Catheter replaced today before cultures because it had been in place for four weeks; urine culture from the new catheter; blood cultures taken.
Ceftriaxone 1 g intramuscularly now, then cefpodoxime 200 mg by mouth twice daily to complete 7 days, adjusted to the culture result.
A fluoroquinolone is avoided (delirium, tendon rupture, and resistance in older adults), and nitrofurantoin is not suitable for a febrile infection.
Acetaminophen 1 g up to every 6 hours as needed, no more than 3 g a day; drink to thirst.
Nurse telephone call tomorrow and in 48 hours with the culture result.

Chronic urinary retention on an indwelling catheter (R33.8). The trial without catheter planned for six weeks should wait until the infection is treated. [S]
Keep the planned trial without catheter at the six-week visit, two weeks from now, if he is well.
Continue tamsulosin and finasteride; rise slowly while febrile.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of catheter-associated urinary tract infection in adults: 2009 International Clinical Practice Guidelines from the Infectious Diseases Society of America (2009); American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults (2023)

Follow-up: Telephone calls tomorrow and in 48 hours. Go to the emergency department for confusion, rigors, fainting, vomiting that stops him taking the antibiotic, or a blocked catheter. Six-week review in two weeks. Next scheduled visit 2026-03-31: six-week review with a trial without catheter and a geriatric assessment. [S]
